confirmed.fix: Minimum fix: compute the page calculator and dealValuation from the NACE that loaded deal.mgx. Store that NACE in MgxData (or use deal.mgx.multiples), and do not use the current snapshot.nace, so that the page, the Pipedrive valuation and slide 4 always agree. Also, in refreshDeal for an unpublished deal whose newest version is not approved: when nace or businessId changed, enqueue a write-script job for version n+1 that reloads Asiakastieto and MGX as for version 1 (slide 4 figures and calculator flag, slides 5 and 6, logos, translation). confirmed.problem: After an owner sends the form with 'not interested', the deal becomes Lost, but the video page still shows the calendar, and POST /v/:code/book still accepts a booking. The booking stores meeting_at, writes a meeting_booked event and alert, and queues write-brief. But moveStage does not move a lost deal, so Pipedrive stays Lost and gets no 'Meeting booked' stage. The Inbox Meeting today filter uses dealDone(), which treats every lost deal as done. So the analyst has a real meeting and a written meeting brief that never show in Meeting today, and the deal page still shows the status Lost. The same thing happens in the other order: the owner books first and then sends the form with 'not interested'. markLost sets Lost, and the booked meeting then drops out of the Inbox. Nothing on the page or in the API stops or reports the contradiction.
confirmed.evidence: Scratch vitest run with the server video harness (scratchpad/a4/vt/lost-book.test.ts, temp DB). Code: booking.ts:51-73 bookMeeting checks only `deal.meetingAt !== null`. routes/video/index.ts:172-178 uses requirePublishedLink, which accepts a lost deal. stages.ts moveStage: `if (deal.status === 'lost' || ...) return { moved: false, event }`. views/inbox.ts:25-27 `dealDone = deal.status === 'lost' || ...` and :155 `!dealDone(deal, now) && meetingUpcoming(deal, now)`. write-brief.ts:59 and sweep.ts:57-58 have no lost check, so the brief is still written.

Then each booked, upcoming meeting shows, also on a lost deal. In moveStage (stages.ts:63), when the deal is lost and stage is meeting_booked, still queue the pipedrive-write stage job. verdict.reason: I confirmed this. I ran the auditor's scratch test (scratchpad/a4/vt/lost-book.test.ts, temp DB, server video harness). It printed 'form 200 lost', 'slots 140', 'book 200 status lost meetingAt 2026-09-28T06:00:00.000Z', and inboxDto 3 hours before the meeting gave meeting_today rows []. The code agrees. requirePublishedLink (access.ts:32-35) does not check for lost, and bookMeeting (booking.ts:51-57) checks only meetingAt. moveStage (stages.ts:63) adds the meeting_booked event but returns early for a lost deal, so no pipedrive-write stage job is queued. views/inbox.ts:25-27 dealDone counts every lost deal as done, and :155 uses it for Meeting today. So a booked meeting in the next 24 hours never shows in Meeting today, but PRD Admin panel, Inbox says the group 'shows each deal with a meeting in the next 24 hours'. The reverse order (book first, then the form with not interested) has the same result. The code already allows a lost deal with a meeting (stages.ts:36 reachedStage returns meeting_booked for a lost deal that has meetingAt), so the Inbox is the part that is wrong. rejected.reason: The quoted strings exist (fi.ts:53-66, :233-236, :241; the same lines in sv, nb and da). But they are not a clear violation of the rule, and no user would notice them. The CLAUDE.md rule forbids em dashes, en dashes and 'hyphens used as dashes in prose (e.g., "something - something")'. The example is a spaced dash between parts of a sentence. These strings are short number labels in select and radio options ('20-49', '1-3 milj. euroa'), not prose. The rule also says hyphens in code are fine. The round 1 rules auditor scanned for this pattern and found 'none. All hits are arithmetic.' A hyphen between two numbers is normal in Finnish, Swedish, Norwegian and Danish UI text, so a prospect does not see a defect. The English and German 'to'/'bis' wording is a style choice for those locales, not a rule. The Finnish format.range is a separate calculator template, not a statement that the rule covers ranges (shared.md:30). The proposed fix also makes the labels worse, for example the Finnish staff option '20 ja 49 välillä' in a select. A new test that rejects each digit-hyphen-digit string would enforce a rule that CLAUDE.md does not state.

confirmed.problem: The documented flow is: the analyst clears a script, then clicks Approve, and the approval adds a write-script job that fills the slide. approveDeal permits this. But advance (pipeline.ts:349-353) computes state.reasons before nextStep adds the write-script job, so it stores script_missing in deals.review_reasons, and the reason stays there until the job ends. The round 3 approvalState() now returns 'blocked' for any approved, unpublished version that has a review reason. So right after a successful approval, the Review page shows the success toast 'Approved. The tool makes the missing audio, renders and publishes the link.' and, at the same time, the destructive alert 'Version N is approved but cannot continue. Fix the review reasons above. An edit removes the approval, so approve the version again after the edit.' It also shows a 'Script missing' reason and the progress panel 'Now: Write the scripts'. The version is not blocked: the job fills the slide and the pipeline continues. The alert stays while the job waits in the queue and while the model writes, which can be minutes when the worker renders another video, because the worker runs one job at a time. An analyst who follows the alert edits the script, removes the approval without need, and must approve again. On a published deal (clear a script in v2, then approve) the stale reason also puts the deal in the Inbox Review group with 'Version 2: Slide 5 has no script' and 'Review video'. The deal page then shows 'Version 2 needs your review. The video page shows version 1 until you approve version 2.' for a version that is already approved.
